verifications.claim: The Artemis II rocket is the Space Launch System (SLS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Atop the 300-plus foot-tall Space Launch System (SLS) rocket (R1); Artemis 2 mission successfully lifted off... Space Launch System (SLS) rocket (R3); Rocket Space Launch System (R4); Artemis II rocket... Space Launch System rocket (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly identify the Artemis II rocket as the SLS.

verifications.claim: The Space Launch System (SLS) is built by a consortium of major aerospace companies led by NASA.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No reference mentions a consortium building SLS; NASA leads design but specific contractors for SLS parts are partially named without consortium reference.

verifications.claim: The main core stage of the Space Launch System (SLS) is built by Boeing.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Core stage mentioned (e.g., Michoud Assembly Facility in R4, SLS core stage engines in R3), but no mention of Boeing.

verifications.claim: The twin solid rocket boosters of the Space Launch System (SLS) are produced by Northrop Grumman.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Northrop Grumman developed them by modifying space shuttle boosters. The twin five-segment solid rocket boosters are the largest of their kind in history.
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly states Northrop Grumman produced the SLS twin solid rocket boosters.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule is built by Lockheed Martin.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: R4 explicitly states Lockheed Martin manufactures the Orion spacecraft/capsule.

verifications.claim: The SLS Core Stage is built by Boeing.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Core stage referenced multiple times (R3, R4), but no attribution to Boeing.

verifications.claim: The Solid Rocket Boosters are produced by Northrop Grumman.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Northrop Grumman developed them by modifying space shuttle boosters.
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly attributes SLS solid rocket boosters to Northrop Grumman.

verifications.claim: The RS-25 Engines are built by Aerojet Rocketdyne.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: RS-25 engines mentioned (R3, R4), but no builder specified; only noted as from shuttle program.

verifications.claim: Aerojet Rocketdyne is now part of L3Harris.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No mention of Aerojet Rocketdyne or L3Harris in any reference.

verifications.claim: The Orion Crew Module is built by Lockheed Martin.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Manufacturer Orion: Lockheed Martin; Orion CM-003 Integrity
verifications.reasoning: R4 attributes Orion (including crew module) to Lockheed Martin.

verifications.claim: The European Service Module (ESM) is built by Airbus on behalf of ESA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: service module—built by a European consortium led by Airbus (R3); ESM: Airbus (R4); ESM was built by Airbus... on behalf of the European Space Agency (R5); ESM is built by Airbus on behalf of the European Space Agency (ESA) (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm Airbus builds ESM for ESA.

verifications.claim: The SLS is designed to be the most powerful rocket in the world.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: the most powerful rocket NASA has ever built (R1); SLS will generate more than 8.8 million pounds of thrust at launch—17 percent greater than Apollo’s Saturn V (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe SLS as NASA's most powerful and more thrust than Saturn V, implying world's most powerful, but not explicitly stated as such.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight to take humans around the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Artemis II is the first crewed lunar mission in more than 50 years (R1); first time humans have headed to the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972 (R3); first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972 (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm it as the first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 over 50 years ago.
